text:
jamie: Heads up — since the v2.14 runtime rollout to canary clusters (yesterday 03:20 UTC) we've seen p95 and p99 upticks for short-chat workloads. A couple of support tickets opened (SUP-1234, SUP-1237). Noticed user-facing latency + timeouts. Anyone on call to triage? :eyes:

alex: On it. Which canary cohort, and is this across regions or just us-east-1?

jamie: Primarily canary-cohort-7 (us-east-1). Metric spike at ~03:40 UTC. p95 ~ 1200ms -> 2100ms, p99 ~ 2.3s -> 4.5s. p50 unchanged.

sarah: Adding graphs: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abc/runtime-latency?orgId=1&var-cohort=cohort-7 — looks like tail moves coincide with instances that got the quantization kernel bump.

ops-bot: Deploy event: runtime-service v2.14 rolled to canary-cohort-7 at 2024-11-28T03:18Z by CI (build/6793).

mike: If p50 is flat and tails are up, might be queueing or an unfortunate KV cache cold path. Can we repro with a synthetic steady stream?

jamie: Repro steps I ran from staging: ```bash
# steady 10 qps, seq len 128
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -X POST https://canary-gw.internal/infer -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"short chat message"}' &; sleep 0.1; done
```
I captured a few slow responses with headers: `x-queue-time: 120ms`, `x-kv-cache: miss`, `x-runtime-kernel: quant-fast`

sarah: Interesting that `kv-cache: miss` shows up. We did change kernel selector priority in v2.14 to prefer quant paths for some model shapes which may change cache alignment.

mike: Suggest bisecting the kernel-priority change. Can we roll back that flag in canary and compare? If rollback reduces p99, we have a smoking gun.

jamie: Rolling a rollback to cohort-7 now (flag: runtime.quant_priority=false). Starting a small % (20%) and will feed steady synthetic traffic.

eng-oncall: Noted. Redirecting support tickets to paging channel. If rollback doesn't help, prepare plan B (divert traffic away from quant path, or pin older runtime).

sarah: After the rollback to 20%: p95 in rolled-back hosts -> 900ms, p99 -> 1.1s. In remaining hosts still on v2.14 p99 stayed ~4.2s.

jamie: Rolling rollback to 100% for cohort-7. Observed overall p99 drop to ~1.2s within ~3 minutes of traffic cutover.

mike: That strongly implicates the quant-priority kernel selector. Two hypotheses: 1) quant kernel has a rare slow path (lock contention or memcpy) under certain sequence lengths; 2) it increases KV cache misses due to memory layout changes. Need perf traces.

sarah: Collecting perf traces / flamegraphs from affected instances. If anyone needs SSH access: jump host is `bastion-canary-7`.

jamie: Attaching a trimmed log chunk from a slow request (timestamps redacted):
```
[2024-11-28T03:42:12Z] request_id=abc123 stage=enqueue latency_ms=115
[2024-11-28T03:42:12Z] request_id=abc123 stage=kernel-dispatch kernel=quant-fast dispatch_ms=4
[2024-11-28T03:42:15Z] request_id=abc123 stage=kernel-exec exec_ms=2890 status=ok
[2024-11-28T03:42:15Z] request_id=abc123 stage=postprocess post_ms=23
```

mike: exec_ms=2890 on kernel-exec, wow. That is not a tiny variance. Open a perf profile on that process and check for memcpy, page faults, or thread scheduling. Also check GPU driver logs for any resets.

ops-bot: GPU driver events: no resets reported in the window.

sarah: Perf shows a hotspot in `quant_decode()` where there is a fallback to scalar path when the sequence length mod block_size != 0. We're hitting a scalar inner loop occasionally.

mike: Ok that explains long tail. Fix path: 1) short-term mitigation = prefer fallback to baseline kernel for sequences that mismatch (we can detect seq len and route). 2) mid-term = patch quant kernel to handle non-aligned seq lens fast. 3) update unit tests and add microbench harness.

jamie: For immediate customer relief I've: 
- rolled back the quant-priority change across canary clusters
- filed a support status update to SUP-1234/SUP-1237 with expected fix timeline
- created issue: INF-4456 (quant kernel fallback perf)

alex: Nice. Can we add a runtime probe that emits `x-runtime-path: quant|baseline` on slow responses for easier triage next time?

sarah: Yep, I'll add the probe and an alert rule: If p99 > 1.5s and percent of `x-runtime-path:quant` > 60% then page oncall.

mike: Also add a canary-stage microbenchmark job that runs a sweeping matrix of seq lengths and model shapes every deploy to catch regressions before rollout.

jamie: Created canary smoke job: `ci/canary/quant-smoke` — will run after kernel selector changes.

eng-oncall: Update the playbook: on p95/p99 spike after runtime rollout: 1) verify cohort and region; 2) gather headers/traces; 3) try feature-flag rollback; 4) if rollback helps, abort rollout and open kernel issue; 5) notify support and customers. I'll add to playbook doc.

sarah: Postmortem TODOs: triage INF-4456, add regression suite, add header probe, add alert. I'll own INF-4456.

jamie: Thanks team. Closing the immediate incident — rollback kept customers stable. Follow-ups tracked in INF-4456. :white_check_mark:
